findings.source: RollupCreator.sol:251 for (..) bridgeContracts.sequencerInbox.setIsBatchPoster(deployParams.batchPosters[i], true); (bridgeContracts = the BridgeContracts struct returned by bridgeCreator.createBridge)
findings.issue: The targets of the sequencerInbox/rollup calls are the fields of a struct returned by an earlier call, read back from memory at offsets that sum every previous returndata size; each call target is a several-hundred-character memory expression, and the call loses its function name (P18/P2).
findings.rule: Bind the fields of a decoded return struct when they are decoded (sequencerInbox = ext_call.return_data[k] or a named temporary) and use the temporary as the call target; then resolve the selector (setIsBatchPoster(address,bool)).

notes: Getters, setTemplates, ownership functions reviewed in detail; createRollup by structure (calldata decoding of the nested Config struct, bridge creation, rollup proxy deployment, initialize calls, batch poster loop, validator loop, upgrade executor, deployHelper, event). Source loops: 2, whiles: batchPosters for (632, 'while s < _268' with 'call .. args address(_279), 1') and validators for (667, filling new bool[](n) with true, then setValidator). Implicit loops: 3 calldata decodes with validation (uint64[2], address[] x2), 2 'while idx < 2' re-encodings of uint64[2] (constant trip count), address re-encodings, 1 checked-exponentiation helper (789), 3 bytes copies (P7). P11: 'if s >= cd[..+196..]: revert Panic(50)' under 'while s < _268' with the same length (632-634), and 'if s >= mem[_293]' (668).
summary: Faithful, with both source loops found; createRollup's calls to the freshly created bridge contracts are unreadable because their targets are fields of a returned struct read back from memory at huge computed offsets.
